battle-sphere.notes: Complete Tony Watson article, printed pp42–43 and46, Dragon26 June1979, read with original images. Accurate reference PDF label, not publisher manual. Selection follows both columns and omits unrelated Thief article. Original 1978Sten cover corroborates identity; exact first-player/full phase sequence and some edge cases remain missing. Specific point-scoring MAJOR recorded.

alpha-nature.notes: Original English/French box-base photograph was individually read at full available resolution. It describes two difficulty levels, category/letter play, hurricane/questions and 84-piece reverse-side puzzle, and explicitly lists a separate rules leaflet. It provides neither full setup/turn details nor victory. Box copyright1996 is later than original family1992. No full rules recovered; related Alpha Animals not substituted.

fast-food-franchise.notes: Actual2004timjim.com capture is an unrelated electronics shop. Actual2000prismgames.com capture is Prism Games & Graphics carnival equipment, not established as Prism/TimJim board-game publisher. Public RPGarchive Prism directory has only an unrelated interpersonal-conflict RPG. None is used as source or identity evidence. Literal English/German/French searches yielded catalogue/component/game-description leads, not a usable rulebook. Some search calls failed in transport; searches are not represented as exhaustive.

fire-and-steel.notes: Named target is GDW1978Napoleonic miniatures rules. Search identifies System7 as a related adaptation and Grognard F index lists review/support leads; no original full source was downloaded in this pass. System7, modern Fire&Steel games and unrelated RPGs are not silently substituted. The public RPG Miscellaneous Rules directory was inspected, contains no named match, and other archive branches remain unexhausted.

archive_coverage.notes: Fresh read of Card-board-and-miniature root confirms the same top-level branch structure previously cached; this is not new full-tree coverage. New RPG Miscellaneous Rules/Add-On/Curios listing is limited to its visible top level. No automatic title matches or unrelated medieval rules accepted.
